صَهَّالٌ Neighing, lit. uttering his voice; [or rather that neighs much or often;] an epithet applied to a horse; (JK, * S, Msb, * K;) and so ↓ صَاهِلٌ and ↓ ذُو صَاهِلٍ . (JK. [But these two I find not elsewhere in this sense.]) ―
-b2- [Hence,] بَنَاتُ صَهَّالٍ Horses. (TA in art. بنى. [It should be observed that بَنَات applied to irrational beings is pl. of اِبْنٌ as well as of اِبْنَةٌ.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
